subject: English
topic: Active and Passive Voice — Conversion (W11 B2)

questions.stem:
Choose the correct passive voice:
Active: She writes a letter.

options.option_text: A letter is written by her.
A letter was written by her.
A letter is being written by her.
A letter has been written by her.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Active: She (subject) writes (simple present) a letter (object). Passive: A letter (object becomes subject) is written (am/is/are + past participle for simple present) by her. Pronoun change: 'she' → 'her' (objective case). Result: 'A letter is written by her.' Trap: 'was written' = simple past passive (wrong tense); 'is being written' = present continuous passive; 'has been written' = present perfect passive.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct passive voice:
Active: They were building a new bridge.

options.option_text: A new bridge was built by them.
A new bridge is being built by them.
A new bridge was being built by them.
A new bridge had been built by them.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Active tense: past continuous ('were building'). Passive structure: was/were + being + past participle. Past continuous passive = 'was/were being + past participle'. Subject 'They' → 'by them'. Result: 'A new bridge was being built by them.' Trap: 'was built' = simple past passive (not continuous); 'is being built' = present continuous passive (wrong tense).

questions.stem:
Choose the correct passive voice:
Active: The teacher has explained the lesson.

options.option_text: The lesson is explained by the teacher.
The lesson was explained by the teacher.
The lesson has been explained by the teacher.
The lesson had been explained by the teacher.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Active tense: present perfect ('has explained'). Passive structure: has/have + been + past participle. Result: 'The lesson has been explained by the teacher.' Trap: 'was explained' = simple past passive (not perfect); 'had been explained' = past perfect passive (wrong — active is present perfect, not past perfect).

questions.stem:
Choose the correct active voice:
Passive: The package was delivered by the courier.

options.option_text: The courier delivers the package.
The courier delivered the package.
The courier has delivered the package.
The courier is delivering the package.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Passive: 'was delivered' = simple past passive. Active: simple past → 'delivered'. Subject (agent after 'by') = 'the courier'. Object (original passive subject) = 'the package'. Active: 'The courier delivered the package.' Trap: 'delivers' = simple present (wrong tense); 'has delivered' = present perfect (wrong); 'is delivering' = present continuous (wrong).

questions.stem:
Choose the correct passive voice:
Active: Someone stole his wallet yesterday.

options.option_text: His wallet was stolen yesterday.
His wallet is stolen yesterday.
His wallet had been stolen yesterday.
His wallet was being stolen yesterday.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Active: 'Someone stole' (simple past). When the doer is indefinite ('someone', 'people', 'they'), the 'by' phrase is omitted in passive. Passive: 'His wallet was stolen yesterday.' (The 'by someone' is dropped as redundant). Trap: 'is stolen' = simple present passive (wrong tense — 'yesterday' confirms past); 'had been stolen' = past perfect passive (would require a reference point before it); 'was being stolen' = past continuous passive (implies it was in progress, not completed).

questions.stem:
Choose the correct passive voice:
Active: They will complete the project by Friday.

options.option_text: The project will be completed by Friday.
The project would be completed by Friday.
The project will have been completed by Friday.
The project is completed by Friday.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Active: 'will complete' (future simple). Passive: will + be + past participle. The agent 'They' is dropped (indefinite/unimportant). 'By Friday' = time expression (not agent), so it is retained unchanged. Result: 'The project will be completed by Friday.' Note: 'by them' would also need to be added if the agent matters, but it is omitted here. Trap: 'would be' = conditional (not future simple); 'will have been completed' = future perfect passive (overly complex for simple future).

questions.stem:
Choose the correct passive voice:
Active: Do they speak English here?

options.option_text: Is English spoken here by them?
Is English spoken here?
Was English spoken here?
Does English speak here?

questions.explanation: B is correct. Active: 'Do they speak' (simple present question). Passive: 'Is + object + past participle?' When agent is 'they' (indefinite/general), 'by them' is omitted. Interrogative passive: Is/Are + subject + past participle? Result: 'Is English spoken here?' Trap: 'Is English spoken here by them?' = includes redundant indefinite agent 'by them' (grammatically possible but not standard); 'Was English spoken' = wrong tense (past); 'Does English speak' = wrong direction (English cannot speak).

questions.stem:
Identify the sentence in PASSIVE VOICE:
(A) The children played in the garden.
(B) The book was read by all the students.
(C) The manager will announce the results.
(D) She has been reading for two hours.
questions.explanation: B is correct. (A) 'played' = simple past active (children = subject, doing the action). (B) 'was read by all the students' = past simple passive (book = subject, received the action; students are the agent after 'by'). (C) 'will announce' = future simple active. (D) 'has been reading' = present perfect continuous active (she = subject, doing the reading). Only B is in passive voice (contains 'was' + past participle + 'by').

questions.stem:
Choose the correct passive voice:
Active: He made me do the work.

options.option_text: I was made to do the work by him.
I was made do the work by him.
The work was made to be done by me by him.
I am made to do the work by him.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Special rule: Causative verbs (make, let, have, see, hear + bare infinitive in active) require 'to' in passive. Active: 'made me do' → Passive: 'was made to do'. Structure: I (me→I) was made to do the work by him. The bare infinitive 'do' gains 'to' in the passive. Result: 'I was made to do the work by him.' Trap: 'was made do' = keeps bare infinitive (wrong — passive requires 'to'); 'am made' = wrong tense (present instead of past).

questions.stem: Which sentence CANNOT be converted to passive voice?

options.option_text: She saw a beautiful sunset.
The rain fell all night.
They built a new hospital.
The chef cooked a delicious meal.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Intransitive verbs (verbs with no object) cannot be made passive because there is no object to become the subject. 'The rain fell' — 'fell' is intransitive here (fell = descended, no direct object). You cannot say 'A night was fallen by the rain' — it makes no sense. Compare: A=saw a sunset (saw=transitive, 'sunset' is object → 'A beautiful sunset was seen by her'✓); C=built a hospital ✓; D=cooked a meal ✓. Only B uses an intransitive verb.
